promptLatex: How many of the integers from $1$ to $200$, inclusive, are divisible by neither $3$ nor $5$?
hintLatex: It is easier to count the integers that are divisible by $3$ or by $5$, then subtract.
There are $\lfloor \frac{200}{3} \rfloor = 66$ multiples of $3$ and $40$ multiples of $5$, with $13$ multiples of $15$ counted in both.
solutionLatex:
There are $200$ integers from $1$ to $200$, and the integers we want are the ones outside the union of two families.

The multiples of $3$ number $\lfloor \frac{200}{3} \rfloor = 66$. The multiples of $5$ number $\lfloor \frac{200}{5} \rfloor = 40$. The multiples of both are the multiples of $15$, of which there are $\lfloor \frac{200}{15} \rfloor = 13$, and these have been counted twice.

By inclusion-exclusion the union has $66 + 40 - 13 = 93$ members, so the integers divisible by neither number $200 - 93 = 107$.
